sources.text: For 25 years, XBOX has remained focused on building games players love, and our anniversary year has been a particularly strong example. From Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , to hugely anticipated games like Fable , players have more great games to play on XBOX than ever. Today, The Game Awards has announced this year’s list of nominees and titles across XBOX’s creative teams have earned eight nominations across multiple categories. Outside of gaming, Prime Video’s ‘Fallout’ has been nominated for Best Adaptation. Thank you to all of the teams that brought these great games to players. Voting is now open on The Game Awards’ official site – tune into The Game Awards on December 10 to see if your favorite games from 2026 take home an award. Our publishing partners also received nominations across a range of categories, with many games available to play today with Game Pass. 007 First Light and CONTROL Resonant are both nominated for Game of the Year and playable across devices with XBOX Play Anywhere. Game Pass subscribers can play nominees like Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , No Man’s Sky , and more. See below for the full list of nominees playable on XBOX, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and remember you can vote for your favorites right now over at TheGameAwards.com . In the meantime, many of these titles will be available at their lowest prices yet with XBOX’s Black Friday sale, starting November 19 – find out more here . Congratulations to this year’s incredible nominees!

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 | Critical Consensus
sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early
sources.text: New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early. "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first." For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result. Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it. If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too . If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype
sources.text: Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games. How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling , the next edition of GTA stands alone , a cultural moment so big ( almost ) everybody has been forced to get out of the way . The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI ’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait. At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida, GTA VI ’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered in GTA V with the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 release Red Dead Redemption 2 , while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most mature GTA game Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is the GTA game the studio has been building toward for its entire existence. Let’s start with that new premise. GTA V introduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, and VI takes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the most GTA -possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal. Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough. GTA VI approaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two. What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal in GTA VI is to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet. To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very much GTA . This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived
sources.text: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time . Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players. We finally have more details about GTA VI’s graphics, including that it’s upscaling 1440p to 4K on base PS5 and Xbox Series X, but PSSR2 on the PS5 Pro. AMD’s FSR Upscaling 4 is used to scale the resolution from 720p to 1080p on Series S. Digital Foundry explains how input lag factored into those choices, as well as the differences between platforms , how well it holds to the target 30fps framerate, plus the impact of VRR. With Grand Theft Auto VI set to finally launch tomorrow, November 19th, our long-awaited return to Vice City is nearly here. But after all this time, some of the gear you’ve used in San Andreas might feel out of place on the glamorous streets of Leonidas County. Luckily for you, we’ve gathered a few of our favorite Xbox and PlayStation 5 accessories to help your long gaming sessions run as smoothly as possible. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 Rockstar Games Tips Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. The long wait was totally worth it. It is one of the best games I’ve played in many years and easily the best Grand Theft Auto game ever made. It is also a big, complicated, and deep game, with so much to do and see. So, to help you out, here’s a bunch of tips for players hopping into GTA 6 this week. Don’t worry, no spoilers are included below. Without spoiling anything, there are some incredibly big surprises and really memorable moments buried in this game. I highly recommend that people avoid watching too many videos about GTA 6 ahead of playing it to avoid ruining one particular late-game moment that might be one of my favorite video game surprises in years. Before you rush out the door to do some missions or rob a liquor store, take a moment to grab a bite and a drink. These items will buff your health, stamina, and focus meter, letting you take more damage, run longer, and slow down time more during combat. And hey, don’t assume that just because you’re drinking a soda or eating a hot dog, you have to stop moving or shooting. In GTA 6 , you can move, shoot, run, hold hands, and even drive while holding and eating food. Finally, you can crack a cold one while shooting a rifle. Around the map, you’ll encounter dogs and cats. If you hold the left trigger, you can zoom in on them and then praise and pet them. And you should do this, not just because dogs and cats are great, but also because it buffs your focus and rewards you with some good behavior points toward your criminal profile. In GTA 6 , you can store guns and clothes in your personal car’s trunk. And you should do this, as changing clothes is a great and fast way to lose the attention of the police. You can manage your clothing, create new custom outfits, and store clothes in your trunk at any clothing store with a changing room, so don’t feel like you have to head back home to change your outfits around or remove stuff from your trunk. Just find a store. Also, Rockstar lets you rename your custom outfits using a list of pre-existing words, like clubbing, hunting, or everyday. I recommend doing that to make it easier at a glance to see what everything stored in your trunk actually is without having to put it on and check. When you go out shopping for clothesâand you will likely do that because dressing up is so much fun in this gameâbring both Jason and Lucia. This will let you buy clothing for both of them, try on new items as either character, and modify their current attire. And bonus: Buying clothing for your partner gets you some extra romance points. The world of Leonida is packed with random events and moments that you can encounter while just walking around. These can be as simple as a drug deal going bad, or as complex as someone who needs help finding their missing spouse after a night partying. Often these events will be signaled to the player via shouting or other loud noises. If you hear something like that, click the left and right sticks to activate focus mode and find the source of the commotion, and then go investigate it. I spent many hours making sure to close it first, then realized it closed when you drive away. Plus, it’s just fun to explore the ocean. On Jason and Lucia’s phones, you’ll find an app called Scooter Bros. This lets you manage your owned vehicles, spawn them near you, and even repair them. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Performance Is Mostly Stable, Except On Xbox Series S Where It Can Hit Sub-20FPS
sources.text: With Grand Theft Auto 6 âs world being as big as it is and current consoles being six years old, thereâs naturally a bit of worry about how the game performs on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Our reviewer played the game on a PS5 Pro, considered to be the most powerful console on the market right now, and said that while it runs at 30 frames-per-second most of the time, there were still some noticeable frame drops in crowded areas. But if you havenât bought a PS5 Pro, what can you expect from GTA 6 âs performance? Well, the folks over at Digital Foundry have done what they do best and created some lengthy technical breakdowns of the game, including stress testing it in explosive situations. According to their video, the PS5 Pro tends to hold a pretty solid 30fps, unless you go around making a mess by blowing up a lot of cars at once; in those moments Digital Foundry saw the game dip to around 24fps at its lowest. The base PS5, however, seems to struggle to maintain 30fps in the best of cases, and if you decide to cause a lot of on-screen destruction, those dips are actually sustained until you leave an area.Â On the Xbox side, the Xbox Series X seems to share the same relative stability as the PS5 Pro, with the same frame drops during car chases, crowded scenes, or firefights when things get busier on screen. The big question is how the Xbox Series S, which was originally released in 2020 as a cheaper, lower-powered alternative to the bougie, more expensive consoles of the year, handles GTA 6 . According to Digital Foundry , there are some details that are less prevalent or rendered with lower-res textures, and the resolution is lower, coming in at 720p compared to the 1440p of Series X. The DF video has a number of comparison shots demonstrating how a lot of small details have been downgraded on Series S, but the real difference is that the framerate is, unsurprisingly, struggling the most on the less powerful Xbox. Digital Foundry reports that while 30fps is the target, even the most “typical” play can affect framerate, with standard combat encounters and car chases dropping it to around 25 and the more demanding carnage bringing it down to 20. There’s even a few seconds in the video where it gets down to 18 and 19fps during an explosive shootout. Ultimately, if youâre hoping for the smoothest possible experience, the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X are the unsurprising winners here. A PC version of the game is rumored to launch sometime next year , and I imagine thatâs where folks with high-end builds are going to be able to get smoother, 60fps framerates as Rockstar apparently has no plans to add a Performance Mode to GTA6 on consoles. If youâre running a Series S, maybe try not to cause too much mayhem along the way for best results.Â Though the Xbox Series S provided a more affordable way for people to jump into the next generation of gaming consoles in 2020, as time has gone on and games have gotten more demanding on the hardware, developers have expressed frustration with having to make their games compatible with the device. That's why Warren Spector, best-known for creating the Deus Ex series, said he hopes "GTA 6 is the last of its kind," arguing he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – but Michael "Cromwelp" Douse, publishing lead over at Larian Studios, sees the positive in the new Grand Theft Auto's monumental launch. Responding to Spector's words, he shares his own thoughts about Rockstar's massive release on X . "On the other hand, maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to shit, it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he writes. "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!" I'm inclined to agree here – heck, my entire feed on every social media platform has been all about GTA 6 since critics' reviews went live. It's difficult to argue the influence and impact of Rockstar's new game, regardless of fans' backgrounds, locations, or, well, anything. Grand Theft Auto 6 is everywhere, left, right, and center. The whole thing almost feels reminiscent of Animal Crossing: New Horizons and how it brought folks together during COVID. Here's hoping it reaches even more players soon with a PC release – and, of course, an online mode that rivals that of its predecessor, GTA 5… although I'd say it will, judging by literally every other feature of the game so far. sources.title: A GTA 6 Location Was Teased by Rockstar All the Way Back in 2021 — And What's Inside Was Worth the Wait
sources.text: SPOILER WARNING: This article features details on a GTA 6 Easter egg. Although it won't ruin the game's story or anything like that, we recognize some people want to organically discover and find interesting things on their own. You've been warned! In 2021, Rockstar Games released the somewhat controversial remastered collection of the PS2 era GTA titles. It was... a mess, to say the least. However, one notable thing came from that collection, but fans weren't sure if it actually meant anything. There was a picture of a house in this new version of GTA: San Andreas that wasn't there in the original game, and it didn't look like a location from any other GTA game. Fans theorized this was actually our first look at GTA 6 ... and it turns out, they were right! The house is real. It's located in Leonard County, in the suburb of Belville (shoutout Jared from the GTA mapping community for discovering this). However, that's just the tip of the iceberg. If you approach the house's garage, you can actually break in. Upon entry, it becomes clear this is a lair for some kind of conspiracy theorist. These aren't just ordinary in-universe ramblings — they're from someone who believes they are in a video game. All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server. The house is located in Belville. (https://t.co/hWt1Koz3uz) https://t.co/t2ZsSRPQFI Various notes and writings on the wall point out that they can't leave Lenoida at all. They tried to purchase a ticket to Los Santos and couldn't, nor could they drive out of the state, and instead are planning to get a boat to try and escape. They also noted that there are an extraordinary amount of doppelgangers in reference to NPCs, that there is nothing behind closed doors, their own neighbors can't enter their homes, and that people phase through walls or "glitch." There's also a graph that shows a comically large spike in violent crime and a bunch of 6s written all over the place, likely poking fun at some of the people who drove themselves mad theorizing about this very game. Perhaps one of the most notable bits is that this conspiracy theorist has determined two people, who go by "J" (Jason) and "L" (Lucia), are immune to whatever problems they are experiencing, suggesting they have freedom and autonomy. Ironically, they may have the least amount of autonomy, though, since they are controlled by the player, but they respawn, are largely free of longterm legal consequences, and can cause tons of mayhem, so they're less restricted than NPCs. It's a very silly Easter egg, and one that leans into the absurdity of the GTA community in many ways. It's unclear whether this house was always meant to be like this, or if someone at the studio decided to have some fun with it after they saw how mad it drove fans. Either way, it gave me a good chuckle. In related news, GTA 6 is already shattering all kinds of records despite not being out globally. The game is driving tons of traffic to Twitch, YouTube, and Kick, with millions of people just watching the game. As for its critical reception, GTA 6 got a 10/10 from IGN and its critical praise has been echoed across the industry. In addition to being nominated for Game of the Year , GTA 6 is currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest rated game of all-time on Metacritic . While its position could change as more reviews trickle in over the next few weeks, it's clear this game is a gargantuan hit (though that likely isn't surprising). sources.text: The best things to do first in Grand Theft Auto 6 are all about money management, unlocking open-world activities, and taking good care of Jason's slithery friend. While there's no right or wrong way to play, these tips and tricks should make your first visit to Leonida, specifically Key Lento, more useful and fun. Here's how to spend your first hours in GTA 6 . GTA 6 's story introduction takes a while and can't be skipped, so if you'd like to start a second playthrough (in the future) without having to sit through the opening cinematic, a post-prologue save file is handy. The first missions, which mainly serve as tutorials, are hardly the most entertaining parts of the story, so you may want to save your game after they're done. Your first visit to Jason's house would make a great save point. At the start of your GTA 6 adventure, money is tight. Before you blow it all on weapons and clothes, beware that you'll need your limited funds to meet certain mission objectives, such as saving for the future and buying flowers for your partner. Since there are fewer and less rewarding opportunities to commit crime in the early game compared to mid-game, it's best to save the outrageous spending sprees for later. If you die with cash on hand, you will lose it all. So, as soon as you've received some income from the first missions, place it underneath the loose planks in Jason's bedroom. If Jason dies, the money in his stash remains untouched. While you should certainly take your time to explore side activities and optional missions in GTA 6 , don't do so in the first few hours of playtime. The game takes a while to open up; you can't sell stolen cars, fast travel, or engage in most side activities before you're at least halfway through the first chapter. You won't have many robbery opportunities either. Don't worry, though; the open world will become far more interesting from Chapter 2 onward. While activities are restricted, you should still keep an eye out for events and NPC encounters as soon as you're set free in Leonida. If you hear someone calling you, notice someone getting arrested, or spot anything else that seems out of the ordinary, be sure to engage with it – it won't add to your main mission progress, but it makes the task more fun. Improving your focus stat in GTA 6 is a bit of a chore, but there are two excellent ways to improve your focus early in the game. The first is feeding Jason's pet snake, whose terrarium is placed near the kitchen in his living room. You get 3% focus each time you feed the snake (limited to once per day). The second activity is scoring points at the basketball hoop below Jason's house. The hoop is near the stairs, and the ball is found somewhere nearby, on the ground. You'll score 2% focus per hit, up to five times. It takes a while for the activity to reset (and gather more focus). Why should you do this now instead of later? Well, let's just say you won't always live around a snake and a basketball hoop. Besides, building focus as soon as possible is very useful, as the ability to slow down time and shoot weak spots consumes focus. "Provoke the cops and see what happens" doesn't sound like the best advice, but in GTA 6 , understanding the crime system is very useful. The longer it takes to rob people, steal cars, and escape the police, the higher the chance it'll end badly for you. So, start practicing until things like hot-wiring cars, escaping buildings, making U-turns to lose the cops, knocking out guards, and hitting weak spots become second nature.

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year
sources.text: The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game , Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail. The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom . That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years. While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026 , and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028 . Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post , Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere. In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

sources.title: Far from dead, GTA 6 and Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake are huge wins for single-player gaming
sources.text: Players are still showing up to put themselves first Are single-player games dead? The question comes up plenty as online games proliferate and once-great studios are devastated by layoffs in a frequently changing, shifting industry. But, as many games dodge roll out of the gaming crater that is November thanks to GTA 6 's launch – there's also never been a better time to celebrate the single-player game, and what a massive success they can still be. After all, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives after a 13-year wait… but where is GTA 6 Online? Not here, that's what, and that hasn't stopped Rockstar Games' latest from already raking in an estimated $1.45 billion even in its all-digital form. It's not the only one this month, as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake became the best-selling physical game of 2026 in the US after just one week on shelves – another single-player adventure. The state of single-player gaming can wax and wane, and it's been a hot topic of conversation ever since EA themselves declared them "finished" back in 2010 , back when live service was beginning to dominate and almost every single-player game had a multiplayer component of some sort. In our GTA 6 review , we call it " the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation" with a great single-player story to follow. It's a sentiment that's been hit back on over the years with plenty of massive single-player success. Larian Studios' head Swen Vinke has even explicitly called out the line of thinking, saying the style of game isn't dead, and that "they just have to be good." Likewise, plenty of solo-focused indie games are successful, and left out of an often AAA-dominated conversation Even so, the idea that 'single-player games are dying' has been hard to escape within an industry plagued by layoffs recently. Especially with the sad closure of EA-owned RPG giant BioWare last month , the developer of legendary offline adventures who ended up in the live service mines with Anthem and early versions of Dragon Age: The Veilguard . There's a sense that EA might be part of a self-fulfilling prophecy with their original observation. But, Vinke is correct – games being good certainly help, and few are better than GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time remake. GTA 6 even shares a Metacritic ranking with the original Ocarina of Time, sitting at 99 to be the joint highest rated games ever . It doesn't get much better than that. It's heartening to see big investments like GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time remake pay off. Even if they're such gigantic cultural icons that it feels obvious that players would show up, it's still not something I take completely for granted. I hope that those logging back in for single-player adventures like these two will stick around and remember the joys of solo play for other, less obvious games once they're looking for more. And, even though they're both games in well-known series, I'm also pleased at just how different GTA 6 and Ocarina are while still both finding recent success – a mature crime caper sandbox and a fairy tale adventure for kids (and big kids like me). Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more It all comes after a series of reflective moments about the sustainability of huge online gaming. PlayStation's huge push to spin up multiple live service online games continues to flounder as Fairgames joins its online gaming graveyard . Sure, I've had plenty of great gaming moments playing with friends deep into the night. But, equally precious to me are the times I've been lost in digital worlds on my own, the flickering of a TV pulling me into deep immersion with characters, worlds, and stories that have left a mark on my own soul, that I reflect on day-to-day. The joy of gaming as a medium is the breadth of experiences they can offer, resonating with me just like a good movie or book could while also providing spaces to chill out with pals. So, is single-player gaming dead? Not even close. This November, it's more alive than ever. sources.text: Is the outlaw couple hot together? Or are they running on empty? In GTA 6 you've got a partner in crime, and it's quite a bit different than it was when you were pulling heists with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in the last game. Jason and Lucia aren't just criminal associates, they're a couple, and their romantic relationship is a big part of the story. Jason and Lucia can grow closer or more distant, depending on your actions, behavior, and choices. That goes for everything from story missions to random criminal acts to everyday interactions and activities. Here's how Jason and Lucia's romance works in GTA 6 . There are four levels to Jason and Lucia's relationship that can change depending on how you play and the choices you make, one being the lowest and four being the highest. Here are the levels: When you begin playing as a couple in Chapter 1, your relationship is already a strong one, though it'll still take a while to get it up to 4/4, if that's your goal. Certain actions, activities, and choices will raise your relationship score, and you'll know you've done it when you hear a chime and see a +♥️ appear on the right side of your screen. Here are just a few actions that will add a ♥️ to your score, and there are plenty more: *Note: You can't initiate sex whenever you want, but there are multiple times in GTA 6 when a sex scene is available to you, signified by double hearts over your home icon on the map or with certain limited-time onscreen prompts. What leads to a sex scene? In my playthrough, twice these scenes happened while I was showering as one of the characters and the other asked if they could join me (and you can decide to let them or not). Another was after I reached a major milestone by contributing money to our savings account (hey, financial security is a major turn-on in real life, too!) and there was also a sex scene after a sizable heist. All of these happened while I was at a 4/4 "Hot Together" relationship status. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. You can also lose hearts from your relationship. This didn't happen often in my playthrough, but here's the ones I experienced: According to Rockstar, if you want a strong relationship in GTA 6, you have to play both sides of that relationship. That means not just playing as Jason and doing nice things for Lucia, but also playing as Lucia and treating Jason well. For my playthrough, where I reached the end of the game with a 4/4 "Hot Together" status, my stats show that I played nearly the exact same amount of time as Jason as I did Lucia. Don't worry, this couple isn't joined at the hip. Both Lucia and Jason have missions, storylines, and activities they can (and are sometimes required to) complete alone. You can play plenty of GTA 6 as just a single character running around without the other, just remember to occasionally spend some time with your partner, respond to their texts, and switch to the other character from time to time. But trust me, you'll want to spend lots of time together. Their relationship is fun to take part in, from both sides. Plus, doing crimes as a couple really pays off. It's helpful to have an extra set of hands to point guns at people, do crowd control during robberies, shoot out a cop's tires while driving, and carry off more loot than you could handle if you were rolling solo. I'll be honest: I don't know how the game is different if you have a 4/4 relationship or a 1/4 relationship, because I've only played through the story once at this point, and I kept my relationship as strong as possible for nearly the entire game. We'll know more about the effects of a weak relationship as other players experiment with their relationship status, and we'll update this guide with what we find out. sources.text: How to improve Jason and Lucia’s relationship How does Jason & Lucia’s relationship level work in GTA 6? The biggest change to GTA 6 when compared to previous games in the franchise is the ability to maintain a relationship with the other playable character. This is central to GTA 6 and has a lasting impact on the game as a whole. In this guide, we’ve explained how Jason & Lucia’s works in the game, and how you can improve it. If you’re looking for more GTA 6 Guides, check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub. If you’re looking for GTA 6 guides, our GTA 6 Guide Hub is full of everything you need to know. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Jason and Lucia have four relationship levels in GTA 6. They are: You can check what level your relationship is at any time by opening the Jason and Lucia menu. Do this by pressing the touch pad, and using the bumpers to navigate over to it. You can also check your Jason and Lucia relationship level by holding right ont he Dpad. To build Jason and Lucia’s relationship, you have to spend time together, show affection, and make sure that you’re doing missions together. While there are some things that make a huge difference to your relationship level, like doing main missions as a pair, other smaller things are just as important. Some of the smaller, non-mission things that impact your relationship level are: Other things like pulling off robberies successfully, evading the cops and other Bonnie & Clyde style antics will also giveÂ you a boost to your relationship level. The key to Jason and Lucia’s relationship level is doing as much together as possible. You don’t have to be entirely locked at the hip, infact there are some missions that can only be done my one or the other, but the key is to not ignore the other person for too long. If you hold right on the Dpad, you can send a quick “check in” message which will help maintain the realtionship. Doing sports, like working our or playing basketball together, or doing activities like playing pool together also contribute toÂ your relationship level. If you don’t maintain your relationship level in GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will become distant from each other. GTA 6 will warn you if you’re not spending enough time together, but the game never stops you from doing it entirely. Some unique cutscenes will play if the relationship gets down to the lowest level, at which point you can still rescue the relationship. When you’re at the lowest relationship level, even small acts of affection towards each other can build it back up quickly. There is also one point in the story where you realtionship level will drop by one level, this is scripted and is easy to recover from, so don’t panic. sources.text: Keeping track of your favorite cars in GTA 6 is one of the most important things that you need to learn how to do With over 157 cars and 29 types of bikes available throughout Leonida, understanding how vehicle ownership works in GTA 6 is crucial. Managing the Personal Vehicles of Jason and Lucia is a major priority as they'll be your main mode of transportation around the world. GTA 6 also handles unowned vehicles, destroyed vehicles, and impounded vehicles in slightly different ways, and the same goes for storing any of your favorites too. So for all things Personal Vehicle-related this car ownership guide will get you up to speed quickly on how vehicles work in GTA 6. A Personal Vehicle in GTA 6 is the car you are legally registered to ride. Both Jason and Lucia can have their own personal vehicle to call their own, but first they need to be registered (which can be costly, depending on the make and model of the car or bike). The benefit of investing in a personal vehicle in GTA 6 is that they can always be recovered via the ScooterBros app on your phone if they are lost or destroyed. You're also able to manage your loadout in GTA 6 from the trunk of these vehicles, change your outfit to lower Appearance heat, and store key items such as stash bags and any spoils from hunting trips. Helpfully, the location of your personal vehicle is always marked on the map. Just open up the GTA 6 Index and scroll to the Personal tab, which is where you'll find your car. Businesses such as Pay 'n' Sprays (as well as key contacts, once you've unlocked the relevant GTA 6 mission) will register an unowned vehicle as your personal vehicle for a fee. This can be pretty costly, depending on the make and model of the vehicle – and you won't be able to register a vehicle with a standard or advanced tracker until you've progressed far enough in the story. Locate a local Pay 'n' Spray by heading to the Vehicles section of the map index, and drive the vehicle you want to register over there. Once you're inside, you'll see the option to register the vehicle and the associated cost. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more It's worth noting that while Jason and Lucia can each have their own personal vehicle at any one time, you can register additional cars and bikes in their names once you purchase new garages. So long as you have the space to store them, you can register the vehicle – and you can summon any registered vehicle whenever you want via the ScooterBros app, a service which will deliver the owned car you want and return the one you don't to storage for a fee. So long as you have the necessary equipment, you can steal pretty much any car that you want to. The last unowned vehicle you drop will be marked on the map under the Personal section of the map index, but unlike Personal Vehicles they can't be recovered if they get destroyed. So, how do you keep an unowned vehicle safe? Beyond paying the price to register it as a personal vehicle, you have two ways to keep an unowned vehicle around. The first is to set it down in a parking space outside of your safehouse, if available. The other is to store it safely in a garage. If your vehicle takes enough damage (and you can't find somewhere to repair your car in GTA ) then it will eventually become undriveable. If this happens to your Personal Vehicle, it can be recovered via the ScooterBros app for a fee. If this happens to an Unowned Vehicle, not only will it be permanently destroyed but you'll also lose access to anything that was stored in its trunk. Sometimes the smartest way to lose your Wanted Level in GTA 6 is to dump your vehicle. This will clear your Vehicle Heat and give you a better chance of escaping, but it will most likely result in the cops impounding it. This will also happen if you're Wasted or Busted by the cops while driving your Personal Vehicle. For a significant fee, you can request the ScooterBros services to recover your ride from the impound lot for you, but this may result in the loss of any stash bags you had hidden in your trunk. If you want a better chance of getting your stuff back, check the Personal section of the map index to see where your vehicle is being held, and then attempt to steal your vehicle back or check nearby cop cars to see if you can recover your loot if they have already removed it from your trunk. © GamesRadar+. not to be reproduced without permission. sources.title: GTA 6's Prologue Can Go Way More Differently Than You Might Think
sources.text: Although it may seem like you’re being overwhelmed from all angles by the police after Lucia’s bungled robbery in GTA 6’s prologue, it is technically possible to evade them and make a clean getaway. That is, until GTA 6’s story immediately course-corrects and sends you back to the scene of the crime. The first time I booted up GTA 6, I was quite overwhelmed by a combination of the dazzling visuals and the urgent need to retrain my brain to click the left stick to sprint rather than hammer the X button. As a result, although I still made a good fist of Lucia’s desperate escape – hustling down a street behind the coffee shop and Ferris Bueller-ing my way over a series of backyard fences – I was eventually brought down by a VCPD officer’s taser bolt that hit me right between the shoulder blades. At this point, the cuffs were slapped onto Lucia’s wrists and the game flash-forwarded back to the present day where GTA 6’s co-protagonist continued her consultation with her correctional counselor in Leonida Penitentiary, and the story launched gloriously into the game’s first chapter. I suspect that most players will have a similar experience during the opening moments of Rockstar’s latest crime epic. However, out of curiosity, I decided to start a fresh save and see if I could get the better of Vice City’s boys in blue. This time, after the annoying good samaritan wrestled Lucia to the floor and the clerk shuttered his window and triggered the alarm, I made a dash across the street and crashed through the gates of an abandoned lot under an overpass. With my Wanted level immediately at two stars and the shriek of sirens rapidly swelling in volume, I frantically scrambled around the edge of a building and… clumsily tripped and fell straight into a canal. This soggy slip-up probably should have sealed my fate, but it actually proved to be my salvation, as I swam up to the surface and straddled a Seashark jet ski that was idly bobbing up and down next to a nearby dock. After briefly fumbling with the new twin-stick hotwiring mechanic I wrenched the throttle and tore off down the waterway, deftly swerving around a couple of fishing boats as the sirens faded into the background and the skyrises of Vice City’s downtown area loomed ahead of me. I was free. Once again the story jumped back to the present, with the counselor asking the orange jumpsuit-wearing Lucia, “You rode a what?” to which Lucia replied, “A Seashark. I mean, it’s Vice City. Everyone’s got one.” This leads me to presume that voice actor Manni L. Perez recorded an alternate line naming literally every possible vehicle in the area that Lucia could have escaped in, because GTA 6 is insane like that and there’s a reason it takes up 200GB of your console’s hard drive space. There’s also a reason that, despite the fact I managed to pierce through the police’s dragnet and find freedom, Lucia still ended up behind bars – and GTA 6 quickly addresses it. Reading her file, the counselor asks, “It says here you got away, but then you went back?” At this point the game once again flashes back to the day of the incident where Lucia, gym bag stuffed with stolen cash still slung around her shoulders, is making her way back to the scene of the crime (for crucial story reasons I won’t spoil here). My two-star Wanted level had changed to red, indicating that although I had lost the cops, they were familiar with my appearance and were still on the lookout for me. However, there didn’t seem to be any officers in my vicinity, so I calmly walked in the direction of the coffee shop and tried not to draw any attention to myself. Before I had a chance to figure out exactly where that annoying beeping sound was coming from, the dye packet hidden in my bag of stolen cash suddenly exploded, splashing pink ink all over Lucia’s workout clothes and immediately alerting every cop in the area. Then came the sirens, then came the patrolmen spilling out from all the nearby sidestreets, then came the heartstopping jolt of a taser bolt as Lucia collapsed and spasmed facedown on the asphalt. The cuffs were once again snapped onto her wrists, and the story shifted back to the present to crash into GTA 6’s first chapter much like it had the first time around. I’m yet to try a third time to try and find out what would have happened if I had managed to return to the coffee shop, or perhaps made a successful escape from the cops a second time, because I’m now neck deep in Jason’s smalltime crime capers and home renovations in the Leonida Keys area. But I just love that from the very first moments that you gain control over one of its characters, GTA 6 feels like it’s been designed to anticipate your every move and instinct and be able to roll with it no matter how the events play out. I can’t wait for the hundreds of hours of experimentation that lay ahead. Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. sources.text: Can you replay any of the missions in GTA 6? Wondering if you can replay missions in GTA 6? Past GTA games have allowed you to replay missions, so now that GTA 6 is out,Â players are wondering if there’s any way to replay what they’ve already played through. In this guide, we’ll explain if you can replay missions in GTA 6, and we’ll let you know exactly what parts of the game you can replay forever. If you’re looking for more comprehensive GTA 6 guides, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub , which includes walkthroughs, beginner’s tips and much more. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. We don’t know if Rockstar will eventually add this feature, but we believe that due to GTA 6’s main missions featuring a lot of different choices that can impact the wider world, including which characters live and die, they’ve decided to not allow players to replay the missions so that the decisions are more impactful. There are some activities in GTA 6 that you can repeat, such as the racing, stunts, pool, and other minigame style missions, but the actual story missions can’t be repeated. Another reason that replaying story missions was removed is likely tied to the medal system from GTA 5 being removed. There are no side objectives on a mission that players need to complete in order to earn a gold medal.Â How you play out the missions is totally up to you. One element of GTA 6’s gameplay that can be repeated is the in-game robberies. These include shops, which will yield a small amount of cashs. The larger bank robberies, which you’ll get access to over the course of the story, can also be repeated. If you’ve recently robbed somewhere, you’ll see on the map that it’s been greyed out. That means that time needs to pass before it is reset, and you can rob it again.

sources.text: GTA 6 is a wild ride – but can you replay missions once you've completed them? Here's something that's a little surprising about Rockstar's long-awaited return to Vice City: There is no way to replay missions in GTA 6. With over 90 main story missions in GTA 6 , some of which are an absolute riot of a time while others feature pretty substantial branching paths that help shape your GTA 6 Criminal Profile system , it's no surprise that many of you are wondering how to replay your favorite moments from the campaign. Sadly, after playing the game for over 100 hours for my GTA 6 review , I can confirm that there's simply no option to do so. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. GTA 5 did let you replay missions easy enough, but that was a way to let you back into key moments to try and complete skill challenges – Rockstar has since moved all of the GTA 6 challenges into its own spot in the progress menu. They are now far broader in scope, and primarily used to unlock GTA 6 cheats once you've wrapped up the story. If you're worried about missing anything or wanting to play key moments from a chapter again, I would recommend that you learn the ins and outs of the GTA 6 save system – this lets you keep and load back into 15 different sessions. sources.title: 25 anos de Xbox: como a Microsoft transformou para sempre a indústria dos games
sources.text: Se você parar pra pensar, vinte e cinco anos é uma idade de alguém considerado jovem, que está chegando no auge da sua vida. Dizem que o auge de alguém pode acontecer aos trinta anos, outros dizem que aos quarenta, mas… será que é possível chegar ao auge aos vinte e cinco anos, ou até antes disso? Com o aniversário da Xbox agora, dia 15 de novembro, nós do Voxl resolvemos contar não só a história de uma das empresas mais importantes do mundo dos games, mas sim explicar como o Xbox mudou a indústria dos videogames: como a marca mudou ao longo dessas duas décadas e meia? O que ela representa para quem joga hoje? Quais suas influências que moldaram a indústria dos jogos, e o mais importante – será que ainda dá tempo de voltar aos seus tempos de glória? Se você, assim como a gente, também ama videogames, já deve saber que a década de noventa é considerada como uma das mais importantes da história dos jogos eletrônicos. Além da continuidade da quarta geração de consoles, que teve como principais destaques o Super Nintendo e o Mega Drive (os famosos 14 bits). Também começamos a ver não só uma evolução rápida de gráficos, como também a transição do 2D para o 3D nos jogos, com o lançamento de consoles como o Playstation 1 e o Nintendo 64, que deram o start para a quinta geração de consoles. Embora o processamento em 3D estivesse começando a ganhar maior popularidade nos consoles, a história era outra nos computadores: com um sistema operacional robusto e conhecido pelos usuários, a Microsoft já dominava o mercado de computadores. O Windows 95 já estava ficando popular em diversos lares pelo mundo, e junto dele, em setembro de 95, vinha também o DirectX: um conjunto de ferramentas e APIs do Windows que serve de intermediário entre os programas do computador e o hardware do computador, com foco principal na GPU e na CPU. Embora pudesse ser usada para desenvolvimento de jogos, o DirectX recebeu olhares tortos de alguns desenvolvedores na época por ser “simples demais” de ser usado. Já com o Playstation 1 e o Nintendo 64 fazendo um grande sucesso de vendas, Otto Berkes, um dos engenheiros líderes do DirectX, acreditava num futuro promissor relacionado aos videogames. A essa altura do campeonato, o DirectX já era visto com outros olhos por vários devs, e também por Otto, que sempre foi apaixonado por gráficos e jogos. Com isso, ele recrutou mais três engenheiros (Seamus Blackley, Kevin Bachus e Ted Hase) e fez a seguinte pergunta: e se a gente criasse uma caixa feita para rodar somente o DirectX para os devs, e além disso – por que não seguir o caminho da Sony, Nintendo e SEGA e também ter um console? Embora hoje em dia a ideia parece ser ótima (e convenhamos, é), o time teve resistência da Microsoft no começo, afinal: como você quer tirar dinheiro de projetos como o Office e o próprio Windows para financiar algo novo, relacionado a jogos eletrônicos? Foi aí que eles contaram com a ajuda de Nat Brown, arquiteto de software na época que deu algumas dicas para o time, sendo a mais importante: vocês precisam criar um nome que chame a atenção. O nome óbvio era DirectX Box, afinal… era o sistema do DirectX dentro de uma caixa, mas eles sabiam que o nome não era legal. Então, o Direct saiu, para ficar somente X Box. Com a ideia pronta, faltava uma pessoa que eles precisavam convencer: Ed Fries, chefe da divisão de games da Microsoft na época. Ed já tinha credibilidade dentro da Microsoft por conta do sucesso de Age of Empires, que fez um sucesso enorme durante seu lançamento em 1997. Com mais um cavaleiro reunido, eles precisavam enfrentar um último boss para que a batalha fosse pra frente: o cofundador e CEO da Microsoft na época, Bill Gates. Mas, tudo estava fácil demais. Após o anúncio do Playstation 2, a empresa começou a dar mais atenção para a ideia, porém junto havia um problema: o Windows CE. Essa versão do sistema foi projetada para funcionar em dispositivos móveis e sistemas embarcados, podendo também ser o sistema base do futuro console da Microsoft – sem contar que a equipe já existia e tinha mais cacife para chefiar o projeto. A batalha estava armada, e Bill iria escolher a melhor ideia. Embora o time do Windows CE tivessem ideias boas, três coisas foram determinantes para que o time DirectX ganhasse a simpatia de Gates: o console teria um disco rígido interno, uma conexão de internet e o protótipo feito pela equipe, que o impressionou, já que foi feito em uma semana e levava apenas seis segundos para ligar (pra quem usou o Windows nessa época, sabe como podia levar até cinco minutos para o sistema funcionar). Após o projeto quase ser barrado pelo presidente executivo da Microsoft na época, Steve Ballmer, a luz verde foi acesa para o nascimento do Xbox. Com apenas onze meses até a maior conferência de desenvolvedores de jogos do mundo, a equipe precisava construir um protótipo do console para apresentar ao público que mais interessava no momento: os que faziam os jogos. Depois de muita discussão sobre o conceito do protótipo, duas semanas sendo esculpido e pesando cerca de dezoito quilos, o primeiro protótipo do Xbox estava pronto. No dia 20 de março de 2000, Bill Gates e Seamus Blackley demonstraram o poder do console para seu público, que ficou maravilhado com as possibilidades para desenvolvimento de jogos que vinham ali. Em vinte meses, começava a campanha para o lançamento do Xbox, e nesse meio tempo uma leva de movimentos que mudariam a história do console ali: sua apresentação oficial na E3, que teve a participação de The Rock, a tentativa de compatibilidade de jogos do Dreamcast rodarem no Xbox, o embrião da parceria com a Bethesda e, enfim, o nascimento da Microsoft Games, que hoje você conhece por Xbox Game Studios. No dia 15 de novembro de 2001, o Xbox foi lançado. Se o primeiro Xbox foi a porta de entrada da Microsoft para o mercado de consoles, foi com a segunda geração que a empresa realmente mostrou que não veio pra brincar. O primeiro videogame da marca conquistou uma boa base
